title: Sound like a native English speaker & use THESE words to describe when you're MAD or SAD in English
channel: Speak English with Bo's Slow English

lines.text: Hello everyone. Welcome to a new episode
of Bow's Slow English. In today's
lesson, I want to go over different ways
to say that you're mad or you're sad. As
a language learner myself, I have a hard
time articulating
my feelings and it's hard to convey your
emotions when you're just saying I am
sad. I am mad. So, hopefully you will
find this useful in your everyday
vocabulary.
Actually, hopefully you don't have to
use these vocabulary words because I
don't want you to be sad or mad, of
course. Please do me a favor first. Hit
like and subscribe to my channel. It's
your way of communicating to me that
you're enjoying this content and that it
is helpful. So, thank you for all of
your support. I think I want to make a
series of emotions and teaching you more
descriptive ways of expressing yourself.
What do you think? Leave a comment and
let me know your thoughts. Let's start
with synonyms for the word sad. Synonyms
are different words that have similar
meaning. Number one, I'm feeling down.
Repeat after me. I'm feeling down. This
is a casual way of saying that you're
sad or depressed. Depressed is another
way of saying you're really, really sad.
Please note, depressed starts with the
letters d e, which is normally
pronounced as d, but in spoken English,
it's depressed, Depressed. Here's an
example of how to use I'm feeling down.
My football team did not make it to the
Super Bowl, so I'm feeling down today.
Number two, I'm heartbroken. Repeat
after me, I'm heartbroken. Heartbroken
is a compound word, heart and broken.
This term means extreme sadness, usually
because of a loss or an emotional event.
For example, unfortunately, my dog
passed away, so I'm feeling heartbroken.
Number three, I'm blue. Repeat after me,
I'm blue. To say I'm blue is a more
poetic or old-fashioned way of saying
that you're sad or melancholic. For
example, I'm blue because my best friend
moved away. Number four, I'm feeling
low. Repeat after me, I'm feeling low.
This means feeling sad or lacking energy
or motivation. For example, I'm feeling
low because the weather has been so gray
and gloomy lately. Number five, I'm
crushed. Repeat after me, I'm crushed.
This means that you're deeply upset or
devastated.
Often by something disappointing or
painful. For example, I'm crushed. I did
not get another callback for that acting
job. Now, let's focus on the word mad
and different ways to express that. I'm
furious. Repeat after me, I'm furious.
This means you're very angry, full of
intense rage. I am furious that my
upstairs neighbor is so loud. Number
two, I'm upset. Repeat after me, I'm
upset. This means emotionally unhappy or
disturbed, but not as strong as angry.
I'm upset that they want to charge me
$5,000 for that. Number three, I'm
livid. Repeat after me,
I'm livid. This means extremely
angry to the point of feeling out of
control. For example, I'm livid. My car
got totaled because that driver was so
negligent. Number four, I'm fuming.
Repeat after me, I'm fuming. This means
that you're so angry that you could
hardly contain your emotions. Like
you're about to explode.
For example, I am fuming that my cat
keeps scratching up my new couch. Number
five, I'm angry beyond words. Repeat
after me, I'm angry beyond words. This
means that you're so angry that you
can't express it properly in words. For
example, I'm angry beyond words that she
tried to cut me off in traffic. Leave in
the comments a few of your own examples
using these terms. Please don't forget
to like this video and subscribe to my
channel. That way I can help you be more
proficient in English and speak with
confidence. Thank you. Bye.
